description: Apple Mobile Device Support (AMDS) from the iTunes installer, without iTunes: the 'Apple Mobile Device Service' (Apple's usbmuxd) that iTunes, iloader, Impactor and similar tools use to reach an iPhone/iPad.
notes: Global install only, from an elevated (admin) shell: scoop install -g Apple-Mobile-Device-Support
Updates and uninstall need admin too.
AMDS is a per-machine MSI: it installs into Program Files\Common Files\Apple, not into the Scoop folder,
and shows up in Settings > Apps. Scoop keeps only the MSI and runs msiexec on install, update and uninstall.
If AMDS is already installed (by iTunes or earlier), an older one is upgraded and a same or newer one is
only taken over: Scoop tracks it from then on. Services that depend on AMDS are paused during the update.
'scoop uninstall' leaves AMDS in place while iTunes is installed, because iTunes needs it.
AMDS has no USB driver. If Windows sees the iPhone/iPad only as a camera/MTP device, install the driver:
scoop install gesu/Apple-Mobile-Drivers-Installer   (then run it as administrator)
msiexec logs: install.log / uninstall.log in the app folder.
pre_install: if (!(is_admin)) { error 'AMDS is a per-machine MSI with a Windows service: run this from an elevated shell.'; break }
if (!$global) { error "AMDS is installed for the whole machine; install it globally: scoop install -g $app"; break }
# Keep only the AMDS MSI; iTunes itself (~175 MB) is not needed.
if (!(Test-Path $msi)) { error "AppleMobileDeviceSupport64.msi is missing from the iTunes installer."; break }
error "AppleMobileDeviceSupport64.msi is not signed by Apple ($($signature.Status))."
pre_uninstall: if (!(is_admin)) { error 'AMDS is a per-machine MSI: run this from an elevated shell.'; break }

script: # On update the new version's installer upgrades the MSI in place; only a real uninstall removes it.
# The version is the AMDS MSI's own; the script downloads iTunes only when Apple's link points to a new release.
